caption:
Today, we raise a glass to Ira Segall as he retires after 17 years with World Wide Stereo and more than 50 years in the audio industry.
 
A musician, recording engineer, and lifelong student of sound, Ira brought a remarkable depth of experience to our team. What made working with him special was the care he took in sharing it.
 
When we started our online business, Ira helped bring the personal experience of our showrooms to customers across the country. He was the voice on the other end of the phone, taking the time to answer questions, talk through a system, and help people find something they would love. His customer reviews say so much about his knowledge, his kindness, and the time he gave people.
 
Ira understood the connection between a great sound system and the way music makes us feel. He has spent a lifetime helping people hear more of what they love, and we’ve been fortunate to share these last 17 years with him.
 
Cheers to Ira Segall. A class act and one of the best out there. Thank you for everything you’ve shared with our team and our customers. Wishing you a wonderful retirement, with plenty of time for the music you love.

What Is Dolby Atmos and Is It Worth It?

Stereo gives you width. Surround sound adds depth. Dolby Atmos adds the third dimension—bringing sound overhead and adding a sense of height and dimension that can make movies, music, and games feel more immersive.

So, is it worth adding? Ken Zelin, Hi-Fi & Home Theater Expert at World Wide Stereo, explains why, when the room permits, his answer is: absolutely.

Know someone building or upgrading a home theater? Send this their way.

👉 Have a question for Ken? Drop it in the comments.

caption:
Sonos has added a second pair of headphones to its lineup.

The new Sonos Ace Ultra sit above the original Ace, adding new 40mm drivers, Adaptive EQ, improved adaptive noise cancellation and up to 35 hours of battery life with ANC turned on.

What most distinguishes them is how they work with the rest of a Sonos system. You can move music between compatible Sonos speakers and the headphones, or move TV sound, including Dolby Atmos, from a compatible Sonos soundbar to the headphones for private listening without disturbing anyone else.

Ben gives us a quick look at what sets the Ace Ultra apart.
